But let’s stick with Locke’s theory for now. Let’s call this the memory theory of survival.
Can we think of cases in which the memory theory and our materialist theories will say different things?

One such case would seem to be a case of complete amnesia. Here it looks like the memory theory will say that the individual whose memories were lost does not survive. By contrast, a materialist theory might well say that individual does survive.

The psychological theorist need not focus exclusively on continuity of memory. Other factors may include: continuity of experience; continuity of plans and projects; continuity of character or personality; being part of the same self-narrative or life-story. There may be others.
